target_customer: Ovarian cancer patients, particularly platinum resistant, via a future therapeutic; near term payers are grant agencies, investors and pharma partners
problem: Ovarian cancer often recurs and resists platinum chemotherapy. Tradewind is developing an antibody against the secreted protein EGFL6 that supports cancer stem cell survival and spread.
business_model: Preclinical biotech developing a therapeutic antibody, funded by grants and equity, with eventual licensing or clinical development

founders.name: Thaddeus Allen
prior_employers: UCSF (studied EGFL6 in lung cancer under a Nobel winning cancer researcher, per TechCrunch)
education: PhD level cancer biologist (institution not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page cites 25 years of cancer research. TechCrunch March 2018 says Allen found Ron Buckanovich's patent and contacted him; that article does not call Buckanovich a founder, though aggregators do.

technical_complexity.rationale: Developing a humanized, affinity matured antibody against a novel target, with unknown receptor, through preclinical and into clinical trials is research grade and regulated.

defensibility.rationale: Novel target with patent position (Allen cites patent portfolio management) and the University of Michigan academic work behind it; clinical and regulatory barriers also protect a successful candidate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent targeting EGFL6. No dated source about the competitor landscape in 2018 was found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch March 2018 and a 2016 University of Michigan study linked EGFL6 to ovarian cancer stem cells and showed a blocking antibody shrank tumors and reduced metastasis in mice; Allen estimated $7M to $10M was needed to reach first stage clinical trials within three years.

branding.domain_note: Uses tradewindbio.com; the exact .com for Tradewind belongs to others.

identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific; describes a multifaceted attack antibody

brand_strength.rationale: Only a TechCrunch demo day article and directory listings; the name is a common trademark term held by unrelated firms.

outcome_analysis: Tradewind remains an early stage preclinical company with two people. It raised no confirmed venture round and its only sourced funding is a $405,552 NIH SBIR grant in 2021, far short of the $7M to $10M Allen said was needed for clinical entry. No 2024 or 2025 news of an IND, trial or shutdown was found, so the story is stalled or slow rather than failed.
notes: Company website returned 503; not worked around. Aggregators list a $120K seed from Y Combinator on 2018-01-04 (CB Insights, Gust, Bouncewatch) but no company or press source confirms it, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Founding year 2017 per YC and CB Insights; some profiles say 2018. Headquarters differs by source. Competitor list empty: searches found later mirvetuximab data but no source dated near the batch; competition in ovarian cancer antibodies existed (for example mirvetuximab trials) but is not documented with a 2018 source. Aggregators call Ron Buckanovich a co-founder; not recorded as founder because neither the YC page nor TechCrunch says so.
